tasks.short: Key supplier and agency invoices into AFAS, match them to orders or hours, post them, and pull lists into Excel.

steps.what: Collect invoices from the AP mailbox and agency portals
Enter invoice header and lines in AFAS

loop.output: supplier, invoice number, date, amounts, VAT lines
loop.check: supplier found by KvK, VAT number and IBAN in AFAS; lines add up to totals; VAT sums match
loop.stop: one pass plus one retry; any failed check sends the invoice to the bookkeeper queue
loop.why_not_simpler: UBL invoices are read by AFAS; PDFs from small suppliers have no fixed layout

steps.what: Match invoice to purchase order, receipt or agency hours
Export lists to Excel for open-item analysis

tasks.design: Turn on AFAS UBL intake and Scan & herken so one-to-one matches post and approve themselves; a small extraction loop handles PDFs that AFAS cannot read and fails to a queue. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform matches the three agencies' invoices to the hours in their portals and AFAS, and a Power BI page replaces the Excel open-items exports.
tasks.previous_blocker: Many PDFs from small suppliers, agency invoices that need hours from three portals, and no one owning match rules or tolerances.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF to line level and books one-to-one matches; AI coding makes the agency hours matcher a few days of work; models read odd PDFs well enough when checked against totals.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portals without a stable export, partial deliveries, and suppliers who keep sending PDFs; the touchless share will be lower than vendors claim.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier or agency is sloppy, and calling them to fix a recurring error at the source.

ambition.what: Check every agency invoice line against worked hours before payment, instead of spot checks.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper works an exception queue instead of keying, and gains the right to set match tolerances and block supplier records with bad master data.

reach.task: Reconcile flex-worker hours with internal shift records
reach.learn: How hours are recorded per site and shift, so agency mismatches can be explained.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and books and approves one-to-one matches
AFAS Scan & herken turns a PDF into an e-invoice, finds supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN, gaps filled by hand
NetSuite case: capture time per invoice fell from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds
Measured touchless shares often disappoint because of own accounts, VAT codes and exceptions

assumptions: Noordhaven runs AFAS Profit 8 or can upgrade
Purchase orders exist for most non-agency spend
A governed data platform or scheduled job host is available
unknowns: Monthly invoice volume and share arriving as UBL
Whether the three agency portals offer hours exports or APIs
Current purchase order discipline per site
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices were UBL, and what share matched one-to-one to an order?
Can each agency portal export hours per worker per week in a machine-readable file?
How many agency invoice lines differed from recorded hours last year, and by how much?

tasks.short: Check postings, VAT codes, ledger accounts and sums for errors, and correct them before close.

steps.what: Pull posting lists and suspense balances from AFAS
Check VAT codes, accounts and cost centres against supplier norms
Find duplicates, IBAN changes and sum errors
Investigate unmatched bank lines and odd postings

loop.input: unmatched CAMT.053 line or flagged posting with candidate open items and payment description
loop.output: proposed match or likely cause with the evidence lines
loop.check: proposed amounts sum exactly to the bank line; the bookkeeper accepts or rejects
loop.stop: top three candidates only; no candidate above threshold goes to the queue as unexplained
loop.why_not_simpler: AFAS rules match on reference, IBAN and invoice number; the leftovers have free-text descriptions and combined payments

tasks.design: A nightly rule job on the AFAS extract checks every posting for VAT code against supplier country and type, account against the supplier's usual account, duplicates and IBAN changes, and posts the hits to a Power BI exception page with a Teams notice. AFAS bank matching stays the first line; a bounded model loop proposes matches for the leftover bank lines, and the bookkeeper accepts and corrects.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks lived in personal Excel sheets run before close, so errors were found weeks late and rules were never written down.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI; rule checks are quick to code; models can read free-text bank descriptions under a sum check.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the norms per supplier and VAT case (reverse charge, intra-EU) and keeping them current; false alarms will need tuning in the first months.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an odd posting is an error, a one-off deal, or a sign of fraud, and talking to the budget holder about it.

ambition.what: Check every posting daily instead of a sample at month end, which takes days off the close.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews a daily exception list and owns the check rules with the controller; they can hold a payment when an IBAN change is not confirmed.

reach.task: Prepare month-end reconciliations and VAT return
reach.learn: Which posting errors cause audit adjustments, so checks target those first.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums; misses go to a person
Since October 2025 banks check payee name against IBAN, but a payer who confirms after a warning is not blocked
Let AP run with people on exceptions and log every decision with its data

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract includes posting lines, VAT codes and supplier master data
The controller will agree to own the rule list with the bookkeepers
unknowns: Number of audit adjustments last year and their cause
Share of bank lines AFAS matches automatically today
Whether IBAN changes are logged with who changed them
research_questions: Which errors drove last year's audit adjustments, and could a rule have caught them?
What share of bank lines stays unmatched after AFAS rules each month?
How many alerts per day would the draft rules raise on three months of history?

tasks.short: Assign ledger account, cost centre, site and VAT code to each invoice per the coding procedure.

steps.what: Read the invoice and decide what was bought for which site

loop.input: invoice lines of a new supplier or a free-text line with no default coding
loop.output: proposed ledger account, cost centre and VAT code with a reason
loop.check: code exists and is allowed for that site; VAT code fits supplier country and reverse-charge flag; confidence above threshold
loop.stop: one proposal per line; below threshold or failed check goes to the bookkeeper
loop.why_not_simpler: Most invoices use supplier defaults; the rest are free-text lines that rules cannot map

steps.what: Look up the coding procedure and past codings
Enter codes on the invoice lines
Chase the budget holder by mail for approval

tasks.design: Set default ledger account, cost centre and VAT code on every regular supplier in AFAS so most invoices code themselves, and move approval from email into the AFAS approval workflow with reminders. A small model loop proposes codes only for new suppliers and free-text lines, checked against the allowed code list, and the bookkeeper confirms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier defaults were never maintained, the procedure sat in a SharePoint document, and approvals ran by email, so coding was done by memory.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS supports supplier defaults and digital approval out of the box; models can classify free-text lines against a fixed code list with a check.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed invoices that span sites or cost types, and budget holders on warehouse shifts who do not open AFAS.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding the right code when an invoice is genuinely unclear and agreeing it with the controller so it stays consistent.

ambition.what: Spend by site and cost type that the FP&A analysts can trust daily, because coding is consistent.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains supplier defaults and the code list instead of coding line by line, and decides when a new supplier gets a default.

reach.task: Build the cost forecast per site
reach.learn: Which cost centres and accounts the forecast relies on, so coding errors that hurt it get fixed first.

evidence.claim: Coding suggested from vendor history for the team to review and confirm
70% of Dutch respondents approve invoices on paper or by email; 43% say this regularly delays payment
Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions block full automation
Intra-EU and reverse-charge purchases may need reporting within 5 days of receipt under ViDA, so slow approval rounds are a risk

assumptions: Most spend comes from a stable set of regular suppliers
Budget holders can use AFAS approval on phone or Pocket app
unknowns: How many active suppliers have defaults set today
Average days from receipt to approval
How many invoices span more than one site
research_questions: What share of last year's invoice lines would a supplier default have coded correctly?
How long do approvals take today, and which budget holders cause most delay?
How often does the bookkeeper change codes after the accountant's review?

tasks.short: Calculate amounts due, payment discounts, late interest, g-rekening splits and balances for payments and customers.

steps.what: Work out due dates and payment discounts for the payment run
Split agency invoices into g-rekening and normal account share
Check payment proposal, IBAN warnings and approve the batch
Calculate late interest and overdue balances on customer accounts
Answer one-off balance and amount questions

tasks.design: Configure payment terms, discounts, dunning and interest calculation in AFAS so the payment proposal and interest invoices come out of the system, with a check that no small supplier gets terms over 30 days. Deterministic code on the agency invoice applies the agreed wage tax and VAT share to the g-rekening and adds it to the payment batch; the bookkeeper approves the batch in Rabobank after reviewing IBAN-name warnings and new payees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Terms and agency percentages were kept in Excel, interest was charged by hand when someone noticed, and the g-rekening split was keyed per invoice.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already does terms, discounts and dunning when set up; the g-rekening split is a few lines of code; the bank IBAN-name check flags wrong payees.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing with sales whether to charge interest to key customers, and keeping agency g-rekening percentages and statements current.
tasks.human_edge: Approving money leaving the bank and deciding when a warning is real; choosing with collections when charging interest hurts a customer relationship.

ambition.what: Apply late-payment interest and early-payment discounts on every eligible invoice instead of when noticed.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper approves batches and maintains terms and g-rekening percentages instead of calculating; they gain a say with collections on interest waivers.

reach.task: Chase overdue customers and agree payment plans
reach.learn: Which customers pay late on purpose, so interest and terms are set per customer.

evidence.claim: Inlener can be liable for agency wage tax and VAT and limits this by paying that share into the agency's g-rekening
Banks check payee name against IBAN since October 2025; a payer who confirms after a warning is not blocked
A large company may not agree more than 30 days with a small supplier
AFAS supports payment terms, discounts and dunning with interest

assumptions: The three agencies have g-rekeningen and agreed percentages
unknowns: Whether interest is charged today at all, and on which customers
Which suppliers count as small under BW 6:119a
research_questions: How much early-payment discount was missed last year?
How much late interest could have been charged on overdue receivables last year, and would sales accept it?
Are g-rekening payments made on every agency invoice today, and with which percentage?

role.altitude: The three bookkeepers move from keying, coding and spreadsheet checks to running exception queues, owning match rules, tolerances, supplier defaults and payment approval with the controller.
reach: Accountant: month-end reconciliations and VAT return
Payroll Specialist: flex-worker hours against shift records
Credit and Collections Officer: interest and payment plans
FP&A Analyst: cost by site for the forecast
skills_to_grow: Writing and tuning match and check rules in AFAS and on the data platform
Supplier master data management and IBAN change control
Reading exception dashboards in Power BI
E-invoicing (UBL, Peppol) and ViDA reporting deadlines
role.ambitious_version: Every supplier and agency invoice is matched, coded and checked the day it arrives, agency hours are verified line by line before payment, and the close loses two to three days because AP and AR errors are found daily instead of at month end.
